subject: Brightline discovery — unit-cost runway, assumptions & invoice sketch
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightline.health>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@brightline.health>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Brightline discovery — unit-cost runway, assumptions & invoice sketch

Hi Samir / Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — helpful to hear your production timeline and the data access constraints. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we’re aligned: 

- Scope: customer support assistant + summarization pipeline (ingest and redact + realtime chat). Estimated avg tokens per request: 120 tokens (prompt + response).
- Traffic profile (your guidance): 75k daily end-user queries at peak, expected to grow 20% q/q for 12 months. That maps to ~270M tokens/month today assuming 120 tokens/request x 75k/day x 30 days.
- Reliability target: 99.8% availability with <400ms tail latency for reads.
- Security: VPC + SOC2 evidence required for procurement — we can provide the standard pack (I’ve cc’d Sergio for SOC2 artifacts).

Budget and unit economics we discussed: you mentioned target unit cost around $/1M tokens that would make the pilot viable. I captured a target of "$450 per 1M tokens" as a reference point from today’s call — please correct me if that’s off.

Attached: brightline_cost_model_v1.xlsx (worksheet with token scenarios), redwood_pricing_calculator.csv (simple slice-based calculator), and a quick invoice sketch (redwood_invoice_sketch.pdf). These are drafts — the model uses two pricing bands: hosted standard models and a discounted dedicated capacity lane for sustained volume. Key levers shown: model family, qps concurrency, batching window, and prefix caching.

Proposed next steps: 
1) You: confirm monthly token range (low / expected / high) and whether we should model a 6- or 12-month pilot.
2) We (Vanessa + Marissa): produce a one-page invoice sketch + 2 scenario cost sheet (conservative / aggressive) and a short note on trade-offs (latency vs unit-cost).
3) Sergio: will send the SOC2/infosec artifact pack after you confirm procurement contact.

Can you confirm the monthly token estimate bands and whether $450/1M tokens is a realistic target to use as baseline? If not, tell us your preferred $/1M target and any hard budget constraints for pilot approval.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min follow-up if it helps (I’m available Tue/Wed next week).

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: brightline_cost_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_pricing_calculator.csv (csv), redwood_invoice_sketch.pdf (PDF)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightline.health>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@brightline.health>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 13:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Brightline discovery — unit-cost runway, assumptions & invoice sketch

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Quick answers from our side: 

- Token bands (monthly):
  - Low: 120M tokens/month (initial pilot, 50k/day)
  - Expected: 270M tokens/month (what we discussed; 75k/day)
  - High: 540M tokens/month (growth / marketing events)

- Pilot length: prefer 6 months to validate user behavior before committing to annual reserved capacity.
- Unit cost target: we’d like total infra + licensing to land at or below $400 per 1M tokens for the pilot. That gets us close to the finance threshold for approval.
- Latency: 400ms tail is ideal; if meeting $400/1M requires trading to a slightly higher tail for a subset of heavy queries, we’re open to a mixed routing plan (hot lane + cold lane) with clear SLAs.

One clarification on the tokens assumptions: most of our queries are short (50–80 tokens) but the summarization responses push the average up. Your model's 120 tokens/request is fine as a working average.

Next: can you share an invoice-level sketch that shows the pilot monthly cost at low/expected/high with the $/1M baseline and the alternative at $450/1M so we can see sensitivity? Also please flag any carrier costs (cloud egress, storage) you put in the model.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, Brightline Health
samir.patel@brightline.health

Subject: Re: Brightline discovery — unit-cost runway, assumptions & invoice sketch

Looping in a quick internal note so we have alignment before Vanessa sends the formal numbers: 

- Samir’s request: show sensitivity for $400/1M (target) and $450/1M (alternate).
- Important: $/1M in our draft includes model inference and platform pass-through costs but excludes persistent storage & egress; we add a line for those as separate optional charges.
- For the 270M tokens/month expected case: at $400/1M tokens that’s $108k/mo; at $450/1M tokens it’s $121.5k/mo — draft invoice should show monthly and effective $/1M after discounts for 6-month commit (we can propose a commitment discount tier).

Action: Marissa — please prepare the 2-scenario sketch (low/expected/high) with a 6-month commitment column and a non-commit pilot column. Highlight where dedicated capacity would materially reduce $/1M at scale (>= 400M tokens/month). I’ll pull the SOC2 summary to attach.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com

Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 17:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Brightline discovery — unit-cost runway, assumptions & invoice sketch

Hi Samir / Elena — attaching the requested sketches.

Summary of attached sketches (redwood_invoice_sketch.pdf + brightline_cost_model_v1.xlsx):
- Pilot (6 months), expected case (270M tokens/month):
  - At $400/1M tokens: $108,000 / month -> $648,000 over 6 months.
  - At $450/1M tokens: $121,500 / month -> $729,000 over 6 months.
- Low and high scenarios included in the spreadsheet; I added a column that shows per-request cost assuming 120 tokens/request and daily traffic.
- Dedication point: dedicated capacity pricing starts to meaningfully reduce unit cost once sustained monthly usage > 400M tokens (sheet shows crossover).
- Line items: inference compute, platform service fee, prefix caching credit (where applicable), optional storage + egress (listed separately).

Next steps: 
- If $400/1M is acceptable, we’ll prepare a formal pilot SOW + DocuSign packet and a proposed 6-month credit/commit discount schedule.
- If you need a lower floor, we can model a hybrid route (hot lane at higher $/1M for latency-sensitive queries + spot lane for batch summarization) and show blended unit cost.

Samir / Elena — can you confirm which option you prefer by EOD Wed (Dec 9)? If confirmed, we’ll route a draft SOW and the DocuSign to your procurement contact (please confirm name/email).

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood_invoice_sketch.pdf, brightline_cost_model_v1.xlsx, redwood_pricing_calculator.csv
